minimal_fixes: none: adaptive_hma_cpp.py imports everything it uses

eligibility.reason: guide 2.1: legacy_reproduction is diagnostic / in-sample reference only

attribution.detail: legacy pos_weight[t] is the position ENTERING bar t, so an entry decided at t appears one bar later in the legacy array; the canonical adapter records the decision bar itself (finding HM-02)

SD-HMA-01.before_semantics: the comment treats the next open as equal to the current close
SD-HMA-01.after_semantics: the engine supplies the actual fill; entry-dependent levels are re-derived from it
SD-HMA-01.expected_effect: levels move whenever the next open gaps

SD-HMA-02.before_semantics: a single pos_weight array mixes the pre-bar position with intrabar exit events
SD-HMA-02.after_semantics: separate fields: position_entering_bar and target_after_close, plus a typed exit event

SD-HMA-03.before_semantics: the RSI recursion returns 100 whenever avg_loss is zero, even when avg_gain is also zero, while the seed returns 50 in that case
SD-HMA-03.after_semantics: the flat case stays 50 throughout the recursion, consistent with the seed
SD-HMA-03.expected_effect: affects only flat segments; applied before any A/B and to every arm identically

SD-HMA-04.before_semantics: mintick is hardcoded to 0.0001 for every instrument
SD-HMA-04.after_semantics: the instrument's real tick size is used; the pip buffer keeps the 10x semantics, versioned
SD-HMA-04.expected_effect: changes the 48-bar high/low buffer per symbol

attribution_rule: every difference must map to a semantic delta. A legacy entry that falls inside the canonical warmup window is attributed to the readiness repairs; an unattributed difference is a defect in the adapter, not a result.
claim_boundary: the legacy tier is diagnostic and in-sample only. Neither side is a performance claim, and a canonical result is never compared against a legacy number as if they were arms.
